text.p: Following are the leading stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- Earthquake measuring 4.7 degrees on the Richter scale that hit Dubrovnik area on Saturday caused landslides, temporarily disrupting traffic on the Adriatic highway, and also inflicted severe damage to the buildings and valuable historical monuments. A series of tremors have been recorded early on Sunday with no damage reported.
- Croatian foreign policy aims for the membership in the Central European Free Trade Organization (CEFTA). Bilateral agreements with six CEFTA members are expected to be signed within a year.

- CAIB, shareholding firm owned by Creditanstal Investment Bank AG, has been granted a licence by the Croatian Government to make deals with securities. This is the first foreign brokerage firm in Croatia. "Euromoney" gave the highest rating to CAIB as the best brokerage firm in Central and Eastern Europe in 1995. and 1996.
- Croatia will not import sugar beet this autumn as it expects to grow 1.2 tons of sugar beet on 26,000 hectars of land which is enough to produce 150,000 tons of sugar.
- Retail prices grew 3.9 percent in March compared to the same month last year. Living costs surged 4.7 percent compared to March 1996., and 4.1 percent compared to the last year.
- Hoteliers in Makarska riviera 'reaped' good results in the preseason. Hotel "Meteor" recorded 22,000 overnights since the beginning of the year. Only April saw the coming of 6.800 visitors.

- Child molesting has become a serious problem in the country. In the last five years 2.053 children fell victims to domestic violence, physical or sexual abuse. In as much as 85 percent of cases, sexual abuse is being committed by parents or very close relatives. This sad statistics is incomplete as most of the crimes remain unreported.
